lead: A centrifuge spins tubes around a spindle. Particles denser than the liquid move outward and settle as a pellet; the liquid left above is the supernatant. Particles lighter than the liquid, such as fat droplets, move inward and float. The outward force is not set by rpm alone. It grows with the square of the speed and with the radius, and the same tube sits at a different radius in a different rotor, so the same rpm gives a different force. Laboratories use this to get serum or plasma from blood, urine sediment for microscopy, and separated blood components for transfusion.
prereq: You need: drag on a particle moving through a fluid, and the blood fractions from 3.4.

blocks.text: Every laboratory protocol needs this calculation. A particle in a spinning tube is pushed outward by a centrifugal field. The field is quoted as relative centrifugal force (RCF): the number of times it is stronger than gravity, g = 9.81 m/s². RCF depends on the radius r, measured in cm from the spindle to the tube bottom, and on the rotor speed in revolutions per minute (rpm).

blocks.where: r is the radius from spindle to tube bottom in cm; rpm is the rotor speed; RCF is a multiple of g.

blocks.text: In SI units RCF = ω²r/g, where ω is angular speed in rad/s and r is in m. Convert rpm to ω with ω = 2π(rpm)/60. Doubling rpm gives four times RCF.

A particle in the tube moves outward until the drag of the liquid balances the push of the field. Stokes' law then gives its settling speed. The sedimentation coefficient s is the speed per unit field, s = v/(ω²r) = d²Δρ/(18η). It is quoted in Svedberg units, 1 S = 10⁻¹³ s. Denser or larger particles have larger s and pellet first; a particle with Δρ below zero moves inward.
v = d² Δρ ω² r / (18 η)
blocks.where: v is the settling speed in m/s; d is the particle diameter in m; Δρ is particle density minus liquid density in kg/m³; ω is the angular speed in rad/s; r is the radius in m; η is the liquid viscosity in Pa·s. Under gravity alone, ω²r is replaced by g.

items: Fixed-angle rotor: tubes sit at a slant; the pellet collects on the outer wall. Good for high-speed spins.
Swing-out or horizontal rotor: buckets swing flat; the pellet collects at the tube bottom and is easy to see.
Bench and microcentrifuge: small volumes; refrigerated versions remove motor heat.
High-speed and ultracentrifuge: higher RCF; an ultracentrifuge spins under vacuum to reduce heating.
Preparative centrifugation collects a pellet. Analytical centrifugation measures the moving boundary during the spin.
Density-gradient separation: Ficoll-Hypaque layers lymphocytes at an interface.

blocks.text: For serum, clotted blood is spun at about 1000–2000 × g for 10 min; on a rotor of 15 cm radius that is about 2400–3500 rpm (worked example 2). Anticoagulated blood spun the same way gives plasma. Urine is spun briefly and the sediment is examined under the microscope. Blood banks separate red cells, platelets and plasma.

items: Balance opposite tubes by weight; imbalance at high speed damages the rotor.
Close and lock the lid; never open while the rotor turns.
Use sealed cups and check tubes for cracks; a broken tube makes an aerosol.

figure.caption: Top view of a swing-out rotor: r is measured from the spindle to the tube bottom. At 2990 rpm the 15 cm rotor gives 1500 × g, but the same speed on a 7.5 cm rotor gives only 750 × g. Right, a spun serum tube: cells and clot pellet outward, serum stays above, fat floats.

examples.question: A tube is held at a radius of 10 cm in a rotor spinning at 4000 rpm. Find the relative centrifugal force. What is the RCF at 8000 rpm?
examples.answer: The RCF is 1788.8 × g at 4000 rpm and 7155.2 × g at 8000 rpm.
examples.check:
r = 10
for rpm in (4000, 8000):
    rcf = 1.118e-5 * r * rpm**2
    print(rcf)

examples.question: A serum protocol asks for 1500 × g. (a) What speed is needed on a swing-out rotor with r = 15 cm? (b) The same tubes are put in a small rotor with r = 7.5 cm at that speed. What RCF do they get?
steps: In the small rotor: RCF = 1.118 × 10⁻⁵ × 7.5 × (2990)² = 1.118 × 10⁻⁵ × 7.5 × 8.94 × 10⁶ = 750 × g, half the force, because the radius is half.
examples.answer: (a) About 3000 rpm (2990 rpm) on the 15 cm rotor. (b) Only 750 × g on the 7.5 cm rotor, so the protocol must be set by RCF, not by rpm.

examples.question: Treat a red cell as a sphere of diameter 8 µm and density 1100 kg/m³ in plasma of density 1025 kg/m³ and viscosity 1.2 × 10⁻³ Pa·s. Find its settling speed (a) under gravity and (b) at 1500 × g.
steps: That is 2.18 × 10⁻⁶ × 3600 = 7.8 × 10⁻³ m per hour, about 8 mm per hour.
(b) At 1500 × g the field is 1500 × 9.81 = 14 715 m/s², so v = 1500 × 2.18 × 10⁻⁶ = 3.3 × 10⁻³ m/s, about 3.3 mm per second.
A single cell would cross a 5 cm column in 50 / 3.3 ≈ 15 s; in whole blood the cells crowd and hinder each other, so packing takes minutes, which is why serum spins last about 10 min.
examples.answer: (a) About 2.2 µm/s, or 8 mm per hour, under gravity. (b) About 3.3 mm/s at 1500 × g, 1500 times faster.

traps: Using the tube diameter instead of the radius from the spindle to the tube bottom.
Quoting rpm as if it were a force: two rotors at the same rpm give different RCF values.
Forgetting to square the speed: doubling rpm gives four times RCF, not twice.
Swapping pellet and supernatant: the pellet is the solid at the wall or bottom.
Skipping the balance step: an unbalanced high-speed rotor can break tubes and release aerosol.

quiz.q: Define RCF. Give its formula and the unit of r.
quiz.a: RCF is the centrifugal force as a multiple of g: RCF = 1.118 × 10⁻⁵ × r × (rpm)², with r in cm.

quiz.q: Why does the same rpm give different RCF on two rotors?
quiz.a: RCF also depends on radius; a larger radius gives larger RCF at the same rpm.

quiz.q: A rotor has r = 8 cm and spins at 6000 rpm. Find RCF.
Rotor A has r = 8 cm, rotor B r = 16 cm, both at 5000 rpm. Compare their RCF.
quiz.a: B has twice the radius, so twice the RCF of A; ratio B:A = 2:1.

quiz.q: What is one Svedberg in seconds?
Convert 3000 rpm to angular speed in rad/s.
Why must opposite tubes be balanced by weight before a high-speed spin?
quiz.a: An imbalance sets up vibration and bearing load; at high speed it can damage the rotor or break tubes.

beyond: Not for the exam. Research ultracentrifuges reach very high RCF and are used to pellet viruses and cell organelles. Analytical ultracentrifugation measures sedimentation coefficients to study protein size and assembly. Microfluidic lab-on-chip devices now spin small discs to separate blood cells. Search for analytical ultracentrifuge, density gradient centrifugation and lab-on-a-disc.
